q.e: Draw all possible Venn diagrams for the three statements; a conclusion follows only if it holds in every one of them.

q.q: 5 friends Faraz, Hina, Mehwish, Rabia, Zainab sit in a row facing north. Rabia sits somewhere to the left of Hina. Mehwish does not sit at either end. Faraz sits immediately to the left of Hina. Zainab does not sit at either end. Mehwish sits somewhere to the left of Zainab. Who sits at the third place from the left end?
q.e: Place the definite clues first (immediate neighbours, ends), then use the 'between' and 'left of' clues to fix the rest; the arrangement is unique.

q.q: A man walks 8 m towards the north. He turns right. Then he walks 5 m. He turns right. Then he walks 8 m. He turns right. Then he walks 20 m. How far is he from the starting point, and in which direction (from the starting point) is he now?
q.e: Net displacement is 15 m west and 0 m south; distance = √(15² + 0²) = 15 m.

q.q: In a certain code language SINDH is written as VHQCK. In the same code, LARKANA will be written as:

q.q: 5 students Asad, Bilal, Danish, Farah, Zainab each have a test on a different day, from Monday to Friday (one test per day). Asad's test is neither on the first nor on the last day. Bilal's test is held on a day between those of Danish and Farah. Zainab's test is held on the day immediately before Danish's. Bilal's test is held earlier in the week than Farah's. Danish's and Asad's tests are on consecutive days. On which day is Bilal's test held?
q.e: Place the definite clues first (immediate neighbours, ends), then use the 'between' and 'left of' clues to fix the rest; the arrangement is unique.

q.q: A solid wooden cube of edge 4 cm has all six faces painted and is then cut into 64 unit cubes. How many of the unit cubes have exactly 0 painted face(s)?
q.e: Classify the unit cubes by position (corners, edges, face centres, interior) and count the painted faces each has.

q.q: One term in the series 2, 5, 10, 27, 58, 121, 248 is wrong. Find the wrong term.
q.e: Rule: each term = previous × 2 + (position of the previous term). The term 10 should have been 12.

q.q: Statements: Some trees are lamps. No coin is a tree. No coin is a file. Conclusions: I. Some files are not trees.  II. No tree is a file.  III. No file is a coin.  IV. No lamp is a coin. Which of the conclusions definitely follow(s)?
o: Only I, II and III follow
Only II, III and IV follow
q.e: Draw all possible Venn diagrams for the three statements; a conclusion follows only if it holds in every one of them.

q.q: Statement: Y > Q ≤ P ≤ S ≤ R ≥ V. Conclusions: I. Y ≤ P  II. P ≤ Q  III. P ≤ R. Which of the conclusions is/are definitely true?
o: Only II and III are true
q.e: A conclusion is definitely true only if it holds for every set of values consistent with the whole chain.

q.q: 6 students Ali, Danish, Kamran, Omar, Salman, Sara each have a test on a different day, from Monday to Saturday (one test per day). Omar's and Danish's tests are on consecutive days. Omar's test is held earlier in the week than Danish's. Kamran's and Sara's tests are on consecutive days. Sara's test is held on a day between those of Danish and Salman. Exactly 2 days separate Kamran's test and Ali's. Danish's test is held earlier in the week than Salman's. Kamran's test is held on a day between those of Sara and Ali. On which day is Salman's test held?
q.e: Place the definite clues first (immediate neighbours, ends), then use the 'between' and 'left of' clues to fix the rest; the arrangement is unique.

q.q: Statement: Q < X < W ≥ V > P. Conclusions: I. V < X  II. P ≤ V  III. Q > P. Which of the conclusions is/are definitely true?
o: Only II and III are true
Only I and II are true
q.e: A conclusion is definitely true only if it holds for every set of values consistent with the whole chain.

q.q: In a row, Farah is 12th from the left and Rabia is 11th from the right. When they exchange places, Farah becomes 16th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
q.e: Rabia's place from the left = 16; so n = 16 + 11 − 1 = 26.
